utterances.text: The bombardments, the shelling certainly appeared to be totally indiscriminate, and the end result was that the town was totally destroyed as a town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have indicated that the city fell on 18th November; can you briefly explain how this came about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I do have some notes which I would like to refer to, if I have your Honour's leave?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, you have the Tribunal's permission.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Over the three months of the sieges, as I have already stated, the city had been almost totally destroyed. It was, you could describe it as a pile of rubble. The JNA had mounted a number of armoured and infantry attacks. The Croatian defence lines had been pushed back further and further, really, effectively, until there was nowhere for them to go. There was a pocket of Croatian resistance in an area called Borovo Naselje, which was just to the south of Vukovar, which was being defended separately. Nearly all of the population had almost gathered round Vukovar Hospital which seemed to be the symbol of resistance and defiance during that three months period. The Croatian defenders had nowhere else to go and really they were faced with no choice but to surrender under overwhelming odds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Inspector Milner, you have mentioned Vukovar Hospital. Can you tell the court something about what was going on at that facility as the battle came to an end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly from the testimony of witnesses that we have interviewed over the period of the investigation, it was clear that the hospital itself seemed to have been made a specific target of the shelling and the bombing by the JNA units. What was once a three storey building with a basement had been so badly bombed and shelled -- at one stage they had white sheets outside with a red crosses to try to get the building exempted from the shelling, and it seemed to be used by aircraft as somewhere to point their targets to pin point where they were going to drop their bombs -- every patient in the hospital had had to go to the basement. That was the only place within the building where the medical staff could actually work properly. When I say "properly", under very extreme conditions. How they actually managed with the number of people that were in the basement is quite incredible when you think about it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you also indicated that a number of people had gathered in the area of the hospital. Are you aware of the reasons why this occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know that there had been negotiations going on between the Serbian -- or the JNA representative, General Raseta, humanitarian organisations and, in particular, the International Committee for the Red Cross. Dr. Bosanac, who was then the Director of Vukovar Hospital, together with representatives of the Vukovar defenders, they had reached an agreement that the hospital and the grounds of the hospital would be a place that would be neutralized, so to speak, that people who were within that area would be evacuated from the hospital and from the grounds and given safe passage to wherever they wanted to go, wherever they chose to go, because at that time there were still some Serbian civilians living within Vukovar itself, living under the same conditions as the Croatian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is your understanding that a lot of these people came to the Vukovar Hospital seeking refuge and safe transit from the area as the JNA occupied the city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There had been communications through the sort of local grapevine by people who were engaged, there that people should gather at the hospital and when the surrender took place, and Vukovar was actually handed over to the JNA, that the evacuation would take place from the hospital and people would be guaranteed a safe passage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point in time did the JNA, in fact, come to the hospital and take control of the facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the JNA actually arrived at the hospital on 19th November; the surrender having been negotiated on 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened once JNA units arrived at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, on 19th November, obviously, they arrived there, there was no resistance. There were many, many people gathered there waiting to be evacuated. The JNA monitored what was going on during the day, how many people were there. They were in the hospital during the night taking names and trying to identify some of the patients who were actually within the hospital at that time in the basement, many of the wounded people and defenders, in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the night of 19th November and until the morning of 20th November, what seemed to be the behaviour of the JNA at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time there was nothing in particular. The JNA behaviour at that stage seemed to be consistent with an army behaving properly and taking care of the people, although some people had been removed, but for what reason we do not know at this stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a point in time when the behaviour of the JNA changed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we know that on 20th November in the morning there was a meeting called where all the hospital employees, all the hospital staff, were ordered to attend. This meeting took place on the ground floor of the hospital building. Major Veselin [ljivan}anin headed the meeting and spoke to all the staff for a considerable amount of time. During that period of time a large number of male patients, together with some hospital employees, were removed from the basement, from the beds where they were being treated and forced to go to the rear entrance of the hospital where they were searched and ordered to mount some five or six buses which were parked just outside the hospital grounds in a street called Gunduliceva Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Inspector Milner, you indicated earlier that there had been an agreement reached regarding international monitoring of the evacuation of the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This evacuation of these men taken out near the emergency entrance, was this conducted in accordance with the agreement that had been reached regarding international monitoring of the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not. The most significant incident on that day is that, apart from having the hospital staff removed from the area where the wounded were being treated so that none of the staff could see who was being removed from the hospital, humanitarian organisations, again in particular a representative of the International Red Cross, tried to gain access to the hospital but was refused. He had, in fact, been told that the route was mined, that it was dangerous, even in spite of the fact that the previous day, on 19th, the hospital had actually been entered by news crews and media and a large number of people had already started to be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These men that were taken outside the emergency entrance, approximately how many men were involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We estimate about 300.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to them after they were taken out of the hospital building itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After they were taken out of the hospital building, they were searched, allegedly for weapons. They were all ordered to get on these five to six buses -- the exact number is not clear but we believe it may have been six -- and as they boarded the buses they waited until everyone had been searched and placed aboard the buses. Once all the people had boarded the buses, the buses then turned around in the street and took a route towards the JNA barracks which were situated in a road called Sajmiste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While on the buses were the men placed under guard or detained in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Each bus had one or two armed guards, JNA soldiers on board the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened once the buses arrived at the JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the buses pulled into the JNA barracks, they pulled into what is described as a circular driveway, so all the buses were lined up in a semi-circle around the central circular drive. Inside the grounds of the barracks there were a large number of what has been described as Serbian irregulars; in other words, not JNAs but people in part uniform who were making threats and gestures of threats and shouting at people, and basically engaged in verbal terrorism towards these men who were on the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point in time while the buses were located at the JNA barracks, were some of the men removed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did this come about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A list had been made of the men, we think a fairly comprehensive list, and a man, one of the accused men, in fact, Captain Miroslav Radi}, Miroslav Miroslav Radi}, got on board each bus in turn with the list and called out names on the list. As each person who was called out identified himself, those particular individuals were removed from the bus and put on board another bus. Eventually, all these men who were put on board the other bus were taken back to Vukovar Hospital. These men were, in the main, hospital employees, people who had been vouched for by people who were actually still at the hospital. We know that when some of these men actually returned to Vukovar Hospital they had to be inspected as they got off the bus, and some of them were actually rejected so they were taken away again and returned to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you have named a couple of individuals in connection with these events already, Major Veselin [ljivan}anin who spoke to the hospital staff and Captain Miroslav Radi} who got on the bus and read out these names. Are you familiar with the military unit that both of these individuals were in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Major Veselin [ljivan}anin was the Commander of the Guards Brigade which was part of the first military district which was actually based in Belgrade, and Captain Miroslav Radi} was the Commander of a special unit within the Military Brigade. Major Veselin [ljivan}anin in actual fact was directly in charge of the Military Police section of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Are you familiar with who was in command of the Brigade as a whole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Colonel Mile Mrk{i} was in charge of that particular Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long approximately did the buses remain at the JNA barracks after they arrived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The estimates will vary, but around two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the buses departed the JNA barracks, where did they go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the buses left the barracks, they turned out in back into Sajmiste Street or Sajmiste in the same direction as they had arrived, continued on that same road which turns into a road called Negoslavci Road. Negoslavci is a village just outside Vukovar, some three kilometres which in fact had been taken over or a house in the Negoslavci had been taken over and used as the sort of command headquarters for Mr. Mile Mrk{i}. Once they left the city, the city boundaries, they travelled about two kilometres south of the town and then turned left on to a small road and travelled through the fields to a place called Ovcara Farm. Ovcara Farm was formally a co-operative farm within the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when the buses arrived at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As the buses arrived outside the main building out of Ovcara which is described as a hangar, the people on board the buses could see a large line or a double line of JNA soldiers together with a large number of these Serb irregulars, as we are describing them. Each bus was unloaded one at a time. As each man got off the bus he was ordered to walk through this tunnel of men. As each person walked through this tunnel of men towards the main doors of the hangar, he was subjected to terrible beatings, kickings, hitting with rifle butts. Any jewellery that was visible on them was torn off them. All their belongings were taken and deposited outside the doors of the hangar, and each man was then made to go inside the hangar and stand facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened once the men were assembled in the hangar in this manner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After all the buses had been unloaded, the doors of the hangar were closed, but a number of these irregulars went inside the hangar and there an orgy of beatings started to take place. Some individuals were subjected to the most horrific acts by some of these irregular people. Certainly at least two of the individuals that were inside the hangar were described as having been beaten to death with people jumping up and down on top of them, kicking their head, beating with rifle butts, really quite indescribable in terms of horror. At the same time there was an individual going around taking names of all the people who were prisoner inside that hangar. We do have a description from some of the survivors also of a man in uniform who was inside the hangar with a whistle, and after a certain period of time he would below the whistle, the irregulars who had been inside the hangar would then leave and they would be replaced by another lot of these irregulars who would then take over where the first lot of had left off engaged in these horrific acts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea how long these beatings continued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They certainly continued for several hours. As you can imagine, if you had been in this situation all sort of sense and time and reality would leave you totally, but it is clear that it continued until dark. But there was another incident that happened before the beatings finally stopped. During the first couple of hours certain individuals came into the hangar who were either JNA soldiers or were part of the volunteer groups or Serb irregulars and had a look around the people who had been taken prisoner. If these people recognised someone they knew, had been a friend or a colleague, they would identify that person and actually put in a word for him with the commander outside. Who the commander was I cannot say at this time, but certainly nine people were selected to come out of the hangar at one stage and were taken away from Ovcara during that afternoon. But they had to wait outside the hangar and could hear the sounds of these beatings continuing until they actually left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After these men left, the nine or so that were saved by people who knew them, what happened to the remaining men that were left in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as I said, the beatings are described as having continued until certainly the evening. No one has been able to be accurate about the time, but we do know that at some stage there was a generator going that operated the lights, so there was electricity there and the lights were switched on. The person who had made the list of names started calling out names of people, and groups of what is described as between 10 and 20 people were selected to go outside the hangar. Those people never came back. One particular witness who was in the third or fourth group of people -- do you want me to continue with this -- one particular witness who was in the third or fourth group of people to be selected went outside where there was a medium sized lorry with a canvas cover on the back, and he along with some other people was ordered on board the lorry. The lorry had a driver and an armed guard. The armed guard was in the actual cab of the lorry. The canvas on the back of the lorry was pulled down, and the lorry was driven from the hangar at Ovcara out on to a small road which goes towards a place called Grabovo. At some stage alone that road there is a dip, quite a steep dip, in the road which is described as getting flooded in the winter. This particular witness has lived in the Vukovar area all his life, knows the geography of the place very well, and is aware of a dirt track which leads to the left of this road near the dip in the road towards Grabovo. The lorry turns left off the Grabovo Road along a dirt track which has a line of trees to the right and open fields to the left. It was very dark at that time and there was some discussion between two people on the back of the lorry as to whether they should try to escape. The people who were talking about it decided that it would be safer to stay on board in case they got shot. This particular individual decided he was going to try to escape anyway, and managed to squeeze out between the canvas and between the ladder at the back of the lorry and onto the ground and actually made good his escape. He does describe hearing some bullets, some gunfire, within a short time of actually jumping off the lorry, but he is unable to say just how many bullets were fired or what happened thereafter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge has anything of significance been discovered near this location where the witness jumped off the truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in 1992 based, on the directions that had been given by this individual, Dr. Clyde Snow and a team of people from the Physicians for Human Rights went to the location as described near Ovcara and started doing some preliminary excavations, and they discovered what appeared to be the site of a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that time are you aware of any efforts which have been made to fully excavate or exhume the site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On the first visit in 1992 Dr. Snow and his colleagues discovered very quickly two skeletons, and as a result of that discovery went back in 1993 to do a preliminary excavation, what was described as a very large trench which had obviously been machine dug. After digging a test trench they discovered nine skeletons and, according to the research that he carried out at that time, there is evidence that that grave could contain up to 300 bodies. Certainly there were signs from the skeletons that had been found that people had been shot through the head. There were bullets scarrings on trees, and empty shell casings found around the immediate area of the grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any items of jewellery or personal items discovered on the skeletons that they did look at? 2 A. Yes. There was the remains of what was clearly a rosary. There was a gold chain. There was a wooden cross and a metal cross, and there was also what appeared to be something like a hand-made medallion which was attached to a metal chain, and the medallion was inscribed with the words "Bog I Hrvati" which means God and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that time were any other attempts made to fully exhume the site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were attempts made to fully exhume the site, but any further work there was stopped by the Serbian authorities who were then ruling that particular area and are still in occupation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have any efforts been made to identify who the bodies are that are in the grave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only means of identification at the present time has been the pieces of jewellery that were actually recovered. In Zagreb there is an organisation that is named "Mothers of Vukovar" which consists mainly of mothers, wives daughters, of missing men from the Vukovar area. We have instigated enquiries through them to see if we can make an identification of those particular people, but until we get the opportunity to actually exhume the grave properly, it will be impossible to identify properly who these people are that are within the grave. As there are some two and a half thousand people missing, unaccounted for, from the Vukovar area, it is obviously something that we would like to do as quickly as possible, but that is the extent of our identification attempts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time, your Honours, I would like to have Inspector Milner display a series of digital maps on the computer which we will mark as Exhibits 15 through 22. I would ask Inspector Milner to show these maps to the court, indicating the locations of the sites that he has discussed in his testimony, and also to relate to the court the route which the victims were taken from Vukovar Hospital on 20th November 1991. I believe this will appear on the computer monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you should have the map displayed in front of you now, I believe? Here we have a map showing the area of Vukovar town and the area surrounding it. The most significant areas here are pointed out: Vukovar Hospital, the JNA barracks which I referred to, Ovcara hangar where the beatings and at least two murders took place, and the actual grave site itself. Just to enlarge that bit slightly, we will go into that in more detail soon. There is a closer view of Vukovar town, and the Hospital up here near the banks of the River Danube and the JNA barracks on the south side of the town. What I would like to show you here, this is the representation of the Hospital building, and this promontory here is a roof which covers what is described as the emergency exit. This emergency exit is situated near the kitchens just along this side of the building. The area here to the right is the front of the hospital. This was where most of the refugees were gathering from the 18th and 19th November in order to be evacuated back to Croatian territory in the main. This emergency exit was where the wounded were removed from the hospital on the morning of the 20th whilst the Hospital staff were being lectured to by Major Veselin [ljivan}anin. There is a downward sloping ramp just alone this area here. I how much you can see the arrow. Coming out here is the Gunduliceva Street. Now the buses were parked alone here. This road is actually a one-way road, and the buses were facing to the left of the screen, if you like, the wrong direction on a one-way road. When the buses were loaded they had to turn around in the street and then head off along this route here. As you will see marked in yellow, Vukovar Hospital at the top. The buses took the direction along this road which seems a pretty straight road here, reaching and crossing the Vuka River. Pardon me for looking here but some of the names are strange for me. There is a square called Marko Oreskovic Square. The buses turn right and follow this route down here towards the JNA barracks here. Now this road is call Sajmiste. This area is where the buses pulled in. This is not the main entrance to the barracks. The main entrance to the barracks is up here. You will see there are two white lines depicted here. That is the main entrance. This is a side entrance to the barracks and the buses pulled in and were in a semi-circle around this particular circular drive. This is where, quite clearly, the JNA were working together with these Serbian irregulars and allowed them to use the barracks and at that stage to start preparing themselves for what was going to happen to the people who were in these buses. When the buses left the JNA barracks they continued on along the same road but which then turns into the Negoslavci Road, and then it does a right turn along here. You see it is getting out into the countryside, into the agricultural area here, then turns a right and along a small road towards Ovcara Farm itself. Perhaps I can enlarge that. This was one of the centres for or the main centre for the Agricultural Co-operative. That was a centre of the workforce until the conflict started in 1991. This road here is the Grabovo Road. As I have described to you, when the lorries left the hangar later on that same night they took this road here, the Grabovo Road, got down to this ravine, there is a dip in the road here, and turn left alone this dirt track and the grave site discovered and partly excavated by Dr. Snow is situated in this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Inspector. Your Honours, at some point in the near future we will have these maps reduced to hard copy and at that time we will tender them to the court. Before I move on, do any members of the court have any questions for Inspector Milner regarding these maps since they are on?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No questions, thank you, Prosecuting Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: At this time then, your Honours, I would like to have a video shown which will be marked as Exhibit 23. This video is a compilation of footage from various sources, but comes primarily from Radio Television, Belgrade, and was their coverage of events that were going on in Vukovar. I would again ask Inspector Milner to narrate as we go through this tape to indicate to the court the locations that we have been discussing and also to point out individuals who are relevant to this case as they appear on the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, you will find that there is no sound track with the majority of this tape, but at a certain stage there will be some sound track and some transcripts have been provided I believe, but I have not got them. What you see here is the city of Vukovar prior to 1991. You will see that Vukovar itself was quite an affluent town, very beautiful, lots of cultural buildings. Some parts of the town actually date back to the 12th Century and many historic monuments; a very rich agricultural community, as well as having lots of natural resources, oil, natural gas and a very thriving factory they called Borovo Factory which employed up to 30,000 people making shoes, leather goods, rubber goods, etc. The town of Vukovar itself had a population in 1991 after a census of some 44,000 people and, as you can see, an attractive place to live. I think the people who actually were residents there were considered to be fairly affluent, certainly in relative terms with the whole of former Yugoslavia. Here we are into 1991 and you can see the differences. Some of the light is adjustable I think. You can see here the absolute devastation that has been caused to a once beautiful city; some of the refugees being taken out. This really depicts the state of the town itself once the JNA had finished their duties there. I think it was described as "liberating" the town. Really the pictures tend to speak for themselves, depicting the needless destruction wanton destruction that has been caused. Some of the cultural buildings will never ever exist again. You can see the main hotel in the background destroyed, all these residential buildings. It does not actually need too many words. In fact, probably the actual scene to visit it is even worse. Some of the tanks as they close in on the town centre. What you will see, it is just an example of shooting where residential buildings are being targeted. There were no military targets at all within that town. The only place that could be described as having any sort of military value was the JNA barracks which was always occupied by the JNA. It was never taken over by any of the Croatian defenders. Churches were a particular target for JNA destruction. Again just examples of wanton indiscriminate shelling, bombing and destruction. This is the water town in the town which is quite a symbol for the people in Vukovar. Some dead bodies on the streets. The bodies here were placed in various locations, people who had actually died in the hospital mainly during the conflict, but because it was so unsafe at one stage to actually go out and bury people, they had to be just laid down in a road to await some stage when they could be buried. This is a mass grave, but it was a mass grave that had been dug by the authorities to dispose of the people that had actually been killed during the conflict. There is nothing mysterious or any significance in that, apart from the numbers of people, innocent civilians, who had been killed. Again some JNA actions. This area itself is an area called Protrovagaro where the main sort of frontline at that particular part of the town is where the JNA set up and controlled one part of the offensive from there. These are mainly irregular JNA soldiers here. During this video you will see clips of people who do not look a bit like JNA soldiers. Again, shots of the destruction. These are people who are obviously not JNA soldiers. You are going to see very shortly a group of people with certain types -- this black hat that is worn by this individual here on the right is described as a Kokarda, they call themselves Chetniks. And just pictures of aimless shooting. The JNA by this time occupied most of the strategic places that there could be for attacking the population. You can get an idea of just how much armoury the JNA were using against a very lightly armed force of defenders of some 1,800 to 2,000 people maximum, and more scenes of destruction. The man in the foreground is Major Veselin [ljivan}anin, and the man pointing his finger by the car is Captain Miroslav Radi}. You can see he was there directing operations at the front line. The people there are a mixture of JNA and paramilitaries and irregulars. That was Veselin Veselin [ljivan}anin talking on the radio to Croatian counterpart because they had the same radio system. As you can imagine, it was all in the same way. You will see Major Veselin [ljivan}anin taking his part in the bombardment of Vukovar here. These are regular JNA soldiers and you can see the difference between those and some of the other individuals. The amount of work that the hospital staff had to do was totally out of proportion to the number of staff that there were there and the conditions they had to work in were unbelievable. This is the basement of Vukovar Hospital and it is not yet full up. As we got nearer to the time of surrender, when more and more casualties were coming into the Hospital, there were sometimes two wounded people sharing a single bed, people sleeping on mattresses underneath beds and people sleeping on shelves; unbelievable conditions and the job that the medical staff did was remarkable. This is Vukovar Hospital or was Vukovar Hospital. There was no way that that amount of damage can be caused accidentally. This was deliberate targeting of civilian locations, a place where they knew there were going to be civilians wounded, helpless and defenceless people. What you are going to see very soon is a hole, a large hole that goes from the roof through every floor of the building. This hole which is shown now was caused by a bomb that was dropped by the JNA Air Force. This bomb was estimated to be in the region of 250 kilos. By some miracle it failed to explode. It landed on the bed of a patient, landing between his legs apparently, and you will see the size of it soon. It was referred to by the hospital staff afterwards later as the "pig". This is the bomb here and the bed that it landed on. It is not all that clear a picture, but I think the picture tells the story. I think if that had exploded there would be a few less witnesses now to what horrors took place in that town in 1991. This is showing the evacuation of people who had gathered at the hospital during the 19th and on 20th. I think the most significant part of these pictures is the fact that you will see there are very, very few young men within these people who are evacuating the town. This area here is the area that I described as the emergency exit where the men prisoners were taken from on the morning of 20th. This area is actually at the front of the Hospital but, as I said, look around and see how many young men there are there. There was a policy of separating all men probably between 15 and 65 as suspected defenders and they were taken away. There is the odd man, but not many. These people have been given the choice of where to go: to go to Croatia or any other country that they actually chose to, but of course their homes are all in Vukovar or were. These are some of the buses that were being used to take them away. What you see here are men that have been separated from the rest of the community. Again, these pictures speak for themselves, victims of the conflict. This was one of the sheets that was used to depict the Hospital as a place that should be exempted from the destruction. You see there is the factory at Borovo Selo which was part of the Vukovar area and some of the men that have been taken prisoner, disarming the men. These people will all be removed and locked up in camps. The great majority of them never ever to be seen again. As I said before, there are some 2,500 people still missing, unaccounted for, with the wives and children waiting for some news. These are the defenders, some of the 1800 people who held out 30,000 of the JNA for some three months. What you will see now is following the surrender. "What is the matter? The colonel knows all the problems. There aren't any problems. I just know that some, that some civilians ... What's the problem? Go on, state the problem, please state the problem? The problem is I can see soldiers walking on the streets. I can see the trucks going on. Look, look, look there. I have opened the bridge to traffic. My colleagues were there. If, sir, your only concern are the interests of people who were in the cellar and whom my soldiers are keeping safe, in that case ... that's all taken care of. If it's no concern of yours that I have had young soldiers killed 18, 19 and 20 years old, then you are not welcome here. And, sir, my own soldiers have been killed here tonight, and, sir, there's a war on here. My soldiers were killed here this evening. There is a war being waged here. We are trying to make sure that you are all safe and left in peace. While you come to me talking of problems. Then if you don't like it here feel free to turn back and go where you do like it and I'm embarrassed to have you treat me this way. Whatever you ask of me I have given it all. .and the court building is next to it. In that building there was yesterday or rather from that building people were firing yesterday, and we saw soldiers taking several hundred rifles from the building, rifles left behind by members of the Croatian National Guard and the Croatian Police when they ran away towards the Hospital where a number of them were hiding. This is now the Hospital entrance and here we see the representatives of the European Mission. You will allow people in these vehicles and this coming into the Hospital and people in white suits with these badges and Red Cross badges to come here, others not. So nobody else can pass through. Not until the wounded are, until the wounded are ready. Those people, those people were right to have done that, no matter whose side they were on. No one as doctor nor any paramedic has reason to fear anything. Yes, go on. There was some misunderstanding this morning with the Red Cross. Has that been sorted out now? There was no misunderstanding on our part, none at all, none at all. Please, gentlemen, first, there was no misunderstanding on our part. I stress once again that this is the zone of corp. protection and that there is a war on and that weather conditions must be respected as well as certain activities carried out by JNA units. And listen, the firing still goes on and that every man and every organisation coming here must be guaranteed safety and security, and everybody must have patience and steady nerves for this is not a time of peace, and this is no ordinary life, but in this kind of life you or anybody else could get killed needlessly at any minute. As far as we are concerned, everything is proceeding according to plan and as agreed. As long as it doesn't happen as it already did yesterday when we got ready 50 bus loads of civilians from Vukovar who wanted to go to Croatia, but the gentleman from Croatia sent them back to Vukovar ... before JNA units liberated Vukovar our barrack was hit by 400 to 500 mortar shells. Last night when we arrested the remaining Ustasha forces and the rest of the citizens, I was proud of my soldiers who had not once tried to take their revenge on someone but extended help as much as was needed, and all our soldiers and all officers are told that it is highly humane and a great honour to help every man and every nation. At the same time, sir, this is a dirty war and no other war in history has been fought in this way. The JNA has sprang from that People’s Army, from that People’s Army which involved World War II fought against fascism together with the rest of the allies. No. Our soldiers are altogether at their positions. They only took part together in the carrying out, in the liberation of the town of Vukovar. Can we make arrangements with the people in the northern command to go and see the hospital? I think I cannot ensure of this right now. Maybe someone else can. That could be solved by, for in that section that the River Vuka can be crossed between us and that operations group north. There are minefields and we are not sure we should take you where you wouldn't be safe. And we have not yet demined the minefields. After a tour of the barracks, he stopped briefly in Negoslavci. There he talked with the commander of the operations group Mile Mrk{i} and the members of his staff. This is the village of Negoslavci three kilometres south of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So Major Veselin [ljivan}anin, Colonel Mile Mrk{i}. "To mark the end of combat actions in the Vukovar region, General Veljko Kadijevic received several of his commanders who had taken part in operations in the area, at the Federal Defence Secretariat. To mark the end of combat actions in the Vukovar region, General Veljko Kadijevic and his aides received the commander of the first military district, Lieutenant General Zivota Panic, the commander of the north operations group, Major General Andrija Biorcevi}, the commander of the south defence groups, Colonel Mile Mrk{i} and the commander of the Air Force unit of the First Air Force Corps of the Air Force and Air Defence, Colonel Branislav Petrovic, all of whom he congratulated on they victory. According to a communique issued by the Federal Defence Secretariat, the reception was also attended by several officers, soldiers volunteers who had particularly distinguished themselves in the heavy fighting in the streets and catacombs of the town which had been fortified for years. In a lengthy conversation on this occasion, General Kadijevic paid tribute to all the participants in the nearly two months of fighting in which a lead Ustasha forces and numerous domestic and foreign mercenaries were trounced and captured. Having pointed out that the combat successes, intrepidity and selflessness that the officers, soldiers and volunteers had displayed in the Vukovar operation, would be a great incentive and inspiration to all the soldiers and officers of the Yugoslav People's Army and Territorial Defence in their fight against resurgent fascism and renewed genocide against the Serbian nation, General Veljko Kadijevic stressed that in a time of victory we remember with all due reverence, all the officers, soldiers whose volunteers lives were built into the victory."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next clip, your Honour, will show the road to Ovcara and the hangar at Ovcara where these prisoners were taken to and beaten, and then we go to the grave site that was described by the survivor and partly excavated by Dr. Clyde Snow. These are the preliminary excavations taking place. You can quite clearly see the skull in the foreground. That is the medallion and the cross that I referred to earlier on in my testimony, and these UNPROFOR soldiers were just examining marks on the trees, bullet scars on the trees. This is Dr. Snow. "We have clear-cut evidence that a mass execution occurred in Ovcara. The evidence so far seems to connect the victims with the patients who disappeared from the hospital at Ovcara on November 20th 1991, so I think this amounts to clear cut evidence of a possible war crime. I cannot think of any other reason why we would find perhaps as many as 200, 250 people executed with gun wounds in a clandestine grave."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the end of the video your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Counsel, maybe after the video we could take a break of 15 minutes before we continue with the questioning or before the judges themselves ask any questions. Yes, Prosecuting Counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I only have one or two further questions, but if your Honour have several and you think a break would be appropriate that is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned. (Short Adjournment)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Prosecuting Counsel, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we would like to show another brief clip from the video that has just been viewed for only about a two-minute portion where earlier you heard the voice of a witness and we are hearing a translation as it was being played, but I would like to have Inspector Milner explain exactly what is going on there. It is a very brief portion, if the court will permit it?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If the extract was not short we would still consider it in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. At this time I would ask that the video be played. Detective, if you could just explain what is going on at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. What you are about to see is a situation where on the bridge over the River Vuka the representative of the International Red Cross Mr. Nicholas Borsinger is attempting to gain access to the hospital grounds and surroundings, having been promised in writing that the evacuation of the hospital would take place under the supervision and monitoring of the international humanitarian organisations. This is the morning of the 20th November and, as we saw earlier on, quite clearly the hospital grounds had been entered on the 19th by Serbian news crews, media crews and by soldiers and other people, yet on the 20th Major Veselin [ljivan}anin is denying access to these people until obviously it becomes convenient for him, and this time is actually the time when the patients, the wounded people from the hospital, are being evacuated by the soldiers of the JNA together with the Serbian paramilitaries. You heard the commentary earlier on how violently Major Veselin [ljivan}anin was objecting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Inspector, can you point out who Major Veselin [ljivan}anin is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Major Veselin [ljivan}anin is the man with the cap in uniform with the moustache. Nicholas Borsinger is the man on the right who is the representative of the International Red Cross and Major Veselin [ljivan}anin is obviously showing his complete authority over what is happening at that place and at that time. You saw also earlier on clips of a meeting between Major Veselin [ljivan}anin and Mr. Cyrus Vance who at that time was a special envoy of the United Nations who was also trying to monitor what was happening within Vukovar and at the hospital in particular, and the same tactics were employed by Major Veselin [ljivan}anin with Mr. Cyrus Vance to stop him and his associates and colleagues having access to what was actually taking place within the hospital grounds at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Detective, after the footage was shown of Major Veselin [ljivan}anin meeting with Cyrus Vance, did Major Veselin [ljivan}anin also meet with Colonel Mile Mrk{i}?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Cyrus Vance met with Colonel Mile Mrk{i}.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The meeting took place in a house that had been commandeered as the JNA Headquarters, for want of a better word, in Negoslavci, in a village which has been described just, three kilometres south of the town of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Detective, at this time do you have any information about the current whereabouts of the three accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we know that Mile Mrk{i} was promoted after the conflict in Vukovar, and he was serving as commander of the army of the so-called Republika Srpska Krajina, the RSK, but after the Croatian offensive in Krajina last year in 1995 he is reported to have fled into Bosnia and is probably now in Belgrade. As for Miroslav Radi}, he is believed very strongly still to be in Belgrade. His family home is in Belgrade, we know that his wife and children. As far as we are aware, he is still serving in the Serbian Army. As for Veselin Veselin [ljivan}anin, he has also been promoted. He is now a Colonel and until very recently was in command of the brigade within the army corps based in Podrica, Montenegro. He is a Montenegrin by descent and by birth I believe. It may well be that through his promotion to full Colonel he is now in Belgrade, but certainly within Serbian territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all three of these individuals are on the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, be it Serbia or Montenegro, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At this time I would like to show to Inspector Milner Exhibit No. 24. Can you identify this for the court, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a photograph of Miroslav Radi}. That photograph is a printout from a video clip and was actually part of the video that you viewed earlier on.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miroslav Radi}, OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I would like to tender this as Exhibit 24. I would now like to show to Inspector Milner the exhibit we are making as No. 25. Detective, can you identify this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is Major Veselin Veselin [ljivan}anin or Major as he was then and Colonel as he is now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell what the source of this photograph is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again the source of this photograph is, it is a print from the video film transmitted by Belgrade television originally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now to tender this as Exhibit 25. I would now like to show Inspector Milner photographs which we are making as Exhibit 26. Can you identify this document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is a picture of Colonel Mile Mrk{i} when he was attending the ceremony following the fall of Vukovar when a number of JNA and paramilitary officers were being congratulated on their achievements in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again what was the source of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again the source of this photograph was a video film which was originally transmitted by Belgrade television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to tender this as Exhibit 26. Your Honours, as I indicated earlier, Exhibits 15 through 22 with the digital maps which we will submit to the court at a later time and also Exhibit 23 which is the video, but all of those will be available should your Honours like to see them at any other point during the hearing. With that, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Prosecuting Counsel. Before we let Mr. Milner go, maybe Mrs. Odio Benito has some questions. JUDGE ODIO BENITO: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a simple question. Inspector Milner, in your declaration you talk many times of people, refugees, in the hospital in Vukovar, people wandering. Could you tell me if in this case the word "people" means men, women, adults, children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or only men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- actually removed from the hospital were mainly men, but we do have testimony to the fact that there were a few women removed, but we have taken our list of missing people from the official records of the Croatian government, their commission for missing people, and it seems that there has been no official report by relatives of the females that were taken from the hospital at the time. Therefore, they have not been included in our list of people within the indictment. So the majority, I would say 98 per cent, 99 per cent, were men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you talk about people, refugees and we saw many images about a lot of women there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. When I talk about people being taken from the hospital ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You talk about people refugees. It is different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The refugees were in the main all women, children and old men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, do you acknowledge what happened to the women and children and old people remaining in the hospital after 300 men were taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all evacuated in buses mainly through Bosnia and ended up in Croatian territory and are now spread out in various parts of Croatia in refugee places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under the protection of the International Red Cross? 2 A. There was an escort by the Red Cross and ECMM monitors who took the convoys. I know from my interviews of witnesses that the actual evacuation was certainly not made easy by some of the routes that they were forced to take, and a lot of women actually ended up in camps for some period of time varying between a month and three months, but they all eventually ended up in -- I say "all", I beg your pardon, I am wrong saying "all" because a number of people actually died within camps, but the majority of people ended up in safe territory in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, Inspector, what happened with the rest of the men, women, children out of the hospital in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I am aware, your Honour, they were all evacuated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The whole population in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the whole of the population in Vukovar because there were still Serbian people there. A significant part of what was known to be Serbian parts of Vukovar were left relatively unscathed through the bombing. It would seem to be a tactic that only Croatian neighbourhoods were actually targeted, and obviously those people just stayed on this. There are people still living in Vukovar in spite of the devastation. They are all Serbian people. JUDGE ODIO BENITO: Thank you, Inspector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Inspector Milner, I would like to have a few clarifications, although you are very clear and I would like to thank you. First, I gathered clearly from what you said that Mile Mrk{i} Miroslav Radi} and Veselin [ljivan}anin had official roles in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is right. They were officers and they are still?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a way they are still?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can add, if I understood rightly, that the JNA itself was directly involved because you mentioned the barracks of Sajmiste?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these barracks the barracks of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the whole operation was directed from these barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, your Honour. The operation was a combination of several units of the JNA or the former JNA. The barracks themselves in relation to the number of people or number of soldiers, armed forces, that were engaged on the attack or the conflict around Vukovar came from various parts of the First Military Brigade territory. So, there was a corps called the Novi Sad Corps. Now Novi Sad is another town completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And a large proportion of those men were engaged with that conflict as well as units from other towns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they JNA too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All JNA, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All JNA, assisted and reinforced by paramilitary units and volunteers of what has been described as Serb irregulars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also indicated that the Minister of Defence, whatever he is called, congratulated those who accomplished this of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. He was the Minister of -- was it of Serbia, of the Serbian Republic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they still considered themselves the Yugoslav National Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yugoslav National Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Serbian but he was the head of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Head of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any congratulations coming from higher authorities too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing that we have got on record, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It went as high as the Minister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it went as high as the Minister. That was Mr. Kadijevic who was doing the congratulations and obviously he was within the government of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now if we go back to the hospital itself, you mentioned that everyone coming out of the hospital was in search of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they find any weapons within?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I am aware, certainly from the testimony of all the witnesses that we have interviewed, no weapons were found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No weapons were found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No weapons were found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were taken to what we consider the execution area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to go back to these important videos you showed us. In the light of what you said too, you said Vukovar was indiscriminately bombarded and, I note, totally destroyed ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- is that right, during three months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any military sites in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only the JNA barracks at Sajmiste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not Croatian, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Croatian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what we saw, there has been a total destruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indiscriminate destruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the partition of 2,500 or did they flee? You mentioned something like 2,500 people deported?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I mentioned, I talked about 2,500 men ---

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- from Vukovar and the Vukovar area ---

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- who were taken prisoner and ---

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- not from the hospital, from the area in total.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In total?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this destruction of Vukovar and the taking away of the 2,500, was it subject of your enquiry or are you following it up still?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is an ongoing part of our enquiry, your Honour. The team that I am working on is charged with investigating Vukovar and, as you can see yourself, a small indication, it is a huge task and we concentrated our initial investigations on the incidents surrounding Vukovar Hospital and the mass execution at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there is a follow-up concerning Vukovar itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I would just like to take advantage of the question that was asked my colleague, and I would like to ask The Prosecutor's office, because we are within the framework of Rule 61, it is the question of the confirmation of an indictment. The Chamber can ask a number of questions with regard to the contributions made by the witness very efficiently and with great relevancy. This video was very important, so I would like to address The Prosecutor's Office, and it is true, I think this was raised at the moment of the confirmation of the indictment, I would like to be certain that the other aspects of Vukovar are still being dealt with by the Prosecutor's Office. Although this is part of the competence of The Prosecutor's office, we have to ask this question, because in this video we can see both the bombing of Vukovar, which was a major, large scale bombing resulting in a lot of deaths, and another part of video we see the heads, the leaders, if you like, congratulating Veselin [ljivan}anin, Mile Mrk{i} and Miroslav Radi}. So I would like to continue the questioning of the judge who confirmed the indictment to see if in this task we can find out what is going on with regards to all the other aspects of Vukovar. Prosecuting counsel, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, as Detective Milner indicated, there are a number of ongoing investigations of incidents in and around the city of Vukovar; some of these centre on events which happened in the city itself; some of them centre on events which occurred in some of the surrounding communities; also, one of them involving the city itself deals with the destruction of Vukovar. There are a number of enquiries going on and it is impossible at this time to say which ones of those will lead to indictment. We believe, however, that all of the enquiries we are involved in are very promising and they are proceeding, and we hope that they will produce indictments relatively soon.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you for these details. Prosecuting counsel, maybe a last question: You published photos on the video. Have these photos been distributed to the IFOR and to all the authorities, because you produced these as evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is my understanding that they have been. I believe that some of the photographs or all of these photographs have been forwarded to the national authorities. I am not sure if they have, in fact, been forwarded to IFOR because it is our information that these three individuals are not located within the area of responsibility of IFOR. We believe that they are all in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and are not in Bosnia. JUDGE: Thank you, Prosecuting counsel. This detail is very important for the Tribunal. Prosecuting counsel, what are we doing next? I would like to thank the witness and thank him for the clarity of his presentation and the density and the wealth of the documents presented to the Tribunal. We now free you of your obligations here. We thank you very much for your statements. Thank you. The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have the floor, Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, that is the last witness that we are to call today. Your Honours, we will be in a position to call further evidence when witnesses come to The Hague next week on Tuesday, 26th March. There is nothing further that we would wish to put to the Chamber at this stage.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, so we are going to adjourn the current hearing in the framework of this attack on Vukovar until 26th, which is a Tuesday, I believe ---

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- at 10 o'clock for the next part of the hearing, and there is a witness for whom I have signed a protection order. I think this is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So I now address the technical aspects because these protection measures which I have requested require a certain number of technical facilities. So for Tuesday, 26th at 10 o'clock, we need to ensure that we have all the technical facilities available for this hearing for this very special protection. The presiding judges are thanking the interpreters and the technicians for their participation. The hearing is adjourned until the 26th, Tuesday at 10 o'clock. (The hearing was adjourned until Tuesday, 26th March 1996 at 10.00 a.m.) 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
